what_this_is: Offline simulation of the two-stage cascade oracle, composed from committed results files. No inference was run.

cascade_rule.stage_1_bulk: mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-6bit — ground_type under prompt variants B (group-a.v1) and D (group-a.v2), both pushed through the coarse binary map
cascade_rule.stage_2_adjudicator: mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-8bit — ground_type under prompt variant A, consulted only on routed items

routes.bulk_agreement: B and D both commit, to the same side -> that is the label
routes.adjudicated:bd_binary_disagree: B and D both commit, to opposite sides -> adjudicate
routes.adjudicated:b_unmapped_d_committed: B lands on an unmapped value, D commits -> adjudicate
routes.adjudicated:d_unmapped_b_committed: mirror image; not named by the stated rule; empty here
routes.undetermined_at_bulk:both_unmapped: neither bulk answer commits -> the cascade declines rather than escalate on no evidence; empty here

eval_set.note: the accepted-flag truth is carried on every results row as `gradient_truth` / `gradient_truth_conflicted`; this file is where those came from and is not re-read here

inputs.determinism: No timestamp is written. Re-running against the same four input hashes reproduces this file byte for byte.

section_3_vs_gold30.note_on_exact_match: The composed EXACT ground_type is defined even on items where the composed BINARY is undetermined: the reviewer answered from the full six-value vocabulary, so `full_scene` or `pattern_or_texture` is a real answer to the exact question even though it commits to neither side of the binary. On an adjudicated item the exact label is the dense model's; on a bulk-agreed item it is B's (`composed`) or D's (`composed_d_first`) — both are reported because bulk agreement is agreement on the binary, not on the exact value.

vs_reviewer_routed_gold30.population: routed subset, gold-30 with a reviewer binary

bulk_agreement_slice_for_contrast.note: The easy slice the adjudicator never sees. If it scores far above the routed slice, the router is finding the hard items, which is what a router is for.

alternative_routings.note: All five keep the same stage-1 pair (B and D) and differ only in what happens to a routed item. `dense_calls` is what the expensive model would actually be asked, so the cost column is directly comparable.

planning_figures.assumption: orchestrator's planning constants: 2.9 s bulk (both variants), 17.5 s dense

in_file_medians.assumption: medians of exactly the rows composed here; variant D is a longer prompt than B and the dense median exceeds the 17.5 s planning figure

section_5_cost.caveat: Wall time is per-inference generation time on one machine with one model resident. It excludes model load, image decode, and — the item this model does not capture — the fact that a cascade keeps TWO models on disk and swaps between them unless both fit in memory at once.

section_6_caveats.what: The bulk arm and the adjudicator are the same family: mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-6bit and mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-8bit. Same-family: True.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: An adjudicator that shares the bulk model's training data and visual priors is correlated with the thing it is adjudicating. It will tend to make the SAME mistakes on the same images, which is exactly the population routed to it. A truly independent adjudicator (different family, or a human) would be a stronger test of the design and could give a different verdict.

measured_here.reading: This is not a soft worry, it is the dominant finding. The dense adjudicator declines to commit on about half the primary population in general, but on the items where bulk B already declined it declines almost always — it inherits B's 'this is a depicted scene' prior rather than resolving it. That is precisely the 'B unmapped, D commits' route, which is the majority of routed traffic, and it is where the adjudicator contributes nothing.

section_6_caveats.what: The gold-30 is not a random sample. It is the disambiguation set — items picked because the oracle and the accepted flag contradicted each other.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: Absolute rates on it read low for every arm and are NOT comparable to the 137-item primary numbers. Its legitimate use is relative: which arm does better on the items that were already known to be hard. n=30, and only 24 carry a reviewer binary at all.

section_6_caveats.what: The 137-item 'flags' truth is a v2-3 palette a human accepted, not an elicited label of the artwork (eval-set.json meta.groundTruthEpistemology).
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: A low agreement number is not automatically oracle failure — P6 exists because several palettes can be valid for one artwork. The gold-30 exists precisely because this truth is soft.

section_6_caveats.what: Every answer is replayed from a committed results file. The cascade was never actually executed as a pipeline.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: This simulation assumes the three runs are exchangeable with three stages of one run. They were run at different times under different prompt-set loads; all three are temperature 0.0 with constrained decoding, so replay is a fair reconstruction, but it is still a reconstruction.

section_6_caveats.what: Variant D's vocabulary is the same six values as B's, but on these 142 artworks D emitted only flat_field / shaded_field / multiple_distinct_fields — never full_scene, pattern_or_texture, or none_discernible.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: D always commits here, so the 'B unmapped, D commits' route is driven entirely by B, and the two unnamed cells of the rule (D unmapped, and both unmapped) are empty and untested. A different corpus could exercise them. It also means D's high commit rate may be a prompt artefact — a prompt that never says 'I cannot tell' is not the same as one that never needs to.

section_6_caveats.what: In `strict_all_labels` a non-committal answer is scored as 'flat'. Variant D never abstains on this corpus, so it is the only arm that pays nothing for that rule, and it is the arm that wins the strict view.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: The composition beats every component on the committed views and on the common-committed subset, but it does NOT beat D on strict kappa. Whether that is a real loss depends on what an undetermined item costs downstream — a labeller that says 'I don't know' on a third of the corpus is a different product from one that always answers, and no number in this report decides which is wanted.

section_6_caveats.what: The route rate driving the cost model (0.507) is measured on these 142 artworks, which are the eval set, not the 6,900-artwork corpus.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: The eval set was built from artworks with an accepted palette and is not a uniform sample of the corpus. A corpus with more scenes and photographs would push B toward unmapped values and raise the route rate, and with it the cost.

section_6_caveats.what: One decode per (image, variant). Temperature 0.0, but no repeat-decode variance estimate, and no confidence interval anywhere in this report.
section_6_caveats.why_it_matters: Differences of a few items between arms on n=137 are inside the noise a resampling estimate would show. Read the direction, not the third decimal.
